wu: Job Charades: Teacher writes 5 job words (e.g., doctor, teacher, chef, driver, nurse) on slips. Students take turns drawing a slip, miming the job silently, and classmates guess by shouting 'Is he a...?' or 'Is she a...?'
wuAlt: Find Someone Who: Hand out a grid with jobs (e.g., 'Find someone whose father is a doctor'). Students mingle and ask 'Is your father a doctor?' and write names.
Flashcard Quick Review: Show 10 job flashcards one by one. Students shout the job name and use 'a/an' (e.g., 'A doctor!').
pres: Teacher shows 10 job flashcards (doctor, teacher, chef, driver, nurse, engineer, artist, farmer, pilot, waiter) and says 'He is a doctor. She is a teacher.' Elicits 'a/an' rule. Then shows workplace flashcards (hospital, school, restaurant, taxi, office, farm, plane, kitchen) and models 'He works in a hospital. She works at a school. He works on a farm.' Checks understanding with 'Where does a doctor work?'
presAlt: Realia Presentation: Bring props (stethoscope, book, chef's hat). Students guess the job and teacher models sentences.
Storytime: Read a simple story 'Sam the Chef' with pictures, highlighting 'a chef' and 'works in a kitchen'.
prac: Workplace Matching: Students get 10 job cards and 10 workplace cards. They match pairs (e.g., nurse + hospital) and say 'A nurse works in a hospital.' in pairs. Teacher monitors and corrects 'a/an' and 'in/at/on'.
pracAlt: Fill-in-the-Blanks Worksheet: Students complete sentences like 'He is _____ engineer. She works _____ office.' with a/an or in/at/on.
Job Bingo: Teacher calls out 'a doctor' or 'works in a hospital', students cross off the matching picture.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes 3 jobs (e.g., 'He is a pilot. He works on a plane. She is a teacher. She works at a school. He is a farmer. He works in a field.') Students draw and label the jobs and workplaces.
re: Stand Up If...: Teacher calls out 'Stand up if you work in a hospital!' or 'Stand up if you know a teacher!' Students stand up and say 'I know a teacher!' or 'My friend is a doctor!'
prod: Guess the Job: Student A thinks of a job and says 'He works in a hospital. He helps people.' Student B guesses 'Is he a doctor?' Continue in pairs. Teacher models first.
rw: Read and Correct: Students read 5 job ads (e.g., 'We need a nurse. Work in a hospital. We need a teacher. Work at a school.') and circle mistakes in 'a/an' or 'in/at/on'. Then write 3 correct sentences about their own dream job.
st: Halloween Song: Sing 'Five Little Pumpkins' with gestures. End with 'Today we learned about jobs and Halloween. Thank you, class! Goodbye!'
g: Student mimes a job, others guess 'Is he a...?'
Teacher calls out 'works in a hospital', students cross off the picture.
Ask 'Is your mother a teacher?' and write names.
Describe a job with 'He works in a hospital. He helps people.'
Complete sentences with a/an or in/at/on.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more sentences about jobs using 'a/an' and 'in/at/on'.
Support: Use word bank with jobs and workplaces for matching activity.
hw: Describe 3 family members' jobs (e.g., 'My father is a teacher. He works at a school.')
Write a short opinion paragraph: 'Should Oujda celebrate Halloween? Why or why not?'
Draw a picture of your dream job and write 2 sentences about it.
tip: Connect Halloween to local culture by comparing it to Moroccan celebrations like Mawlid al-Nabi or Aid al-Fitr. Ask students to share their opinions on imported festivals vs. traditional ones.
